ArticlesAndMore.admin module

Django admin registrations for ArticlesAndMore.

These are for maintenance/debugging only (e.g. fixing bad data). Regular functionality — creating a Publisher, assigning editors/journalists to one — is handled entirely in the app itself (see views.publisher_create, publisher_assign_self, and publisher_assign_journalist), not here.

class ArticlesAndMore.forms.AssignJournalistForm(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Form

Form used by an editor to assign a journalist to the publisher they’re themselves assigned to.

Only journalists with no publisher_j set are offered, since a journalist can only work for one publisher at a time - the view is responsible for checking the submitting editor actually belongs to the target publisher.

clean()[source]

Hook for doing any extra model-wide validation after clean() has been called on every field by self.clean_fields. Any ValidationError raised by this method will not be associated with a particular field; it will have a special-case association with the field defined by NON_FIELD_ERRORS.

role

A wrapper for a deferred-loading field. When the value is read from this object the first time, the query is executed.

save(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Enforce that a user only ever holds the fields relevant to their current role. clean() rejects an invalid combination when a form calls full_clean() first, but nothing previously stopped a direct .save() (e.g. an admin edit, a script, a role change elsewhere in the app) from leaving stale data on the “wrong” fields for the new role. This clears them unconditionally on every save, so the model’s own persistence layer guarantees the invariant regardless of how it’s saved: a Journalist’s publisher_e is always None, an Editor’s publisher_j is always None, and neither has reader subscriptions — and vice versa, a Reader has neither publisher_j nor publisher_e set.

ArticlesAndMore.notifications module

Notification side-effects that fire when an editor approves an article:

  1. Email every reader subscribed to the article’s author or its publisher.

  2. POST the article to this project’s own /api/approved endpoint, standing in for a real third-party integration while keeping everything local.

Both are called from views.article_approve, right after an article transitions from not-approved to approved.

ArticlesAndMore.notifications.notify_article_approved(article, request)[source]

Run both approval side-effects. Called once, right after an article transitions from not-approved to approved.

ArticlesAndMore.notifications.send_approval_email(article)[source]

Email every subscribed reader that this article has been approved.

ArticlesAndMore.notifications.share_article_externally(article, request)[source]

POST the approved article to this project’s own /api/approved endpoint.

ArticlesAndMore.permissions module

Maps each user role’s Group name to the ArticlesAndMore permission codenames it should hold. sync_role_groups (re)creates the Reader, Journalist, and Editor groups with these permissions after every migrate. sync_user_group keeps each User’s group membership in sync with their role whenever they’re saved (e.g. on registration in AuthApp, or a role change in the admin). Both are connected as signal receivers in ArticlesAndMore/apps.py, so nothing outside this app needs to import ROLE_PERMISSIONS directly.

ArticlesAndMore.permissions.sync_role_groups(sender=None, **kwargs)[source]

(Re)create the Reader, Journalist, and Editor groups with their permissions. Models are imported locally because this also runs as a post_migrate receiver, before the app registry is guaranteed ready.

ArticlesAndMore.permissions.sync_user_group(sender, instance, **kwargs)[source]

Whenever a User is saved, make sure they belong to exactly the Group matching their current role (and none of the other two role groups). Without this, a user’s role field would drift out of sync with the actual Group-based permissions the app checks against.

ArticlesAndMore.tests module

Tests for the ArticlesAndMore app: the /api/articles/… REST API, newsletter web views, and the article-approval notification side effects.

ArticleAPITestCase uses DRF’s APITestCase, which spins up a real (in-memory, per-test) database and lets us make requests through the same URL routing, authentication, and permission machinery a real client would go through — no mocking involved. Each test creates its own users/articles in setUp() and every test runs in its own DB transaction that’s rolled back afterwards, so tests can’t leak state into one another.

Test users are created with User.objects.create_user(…), which triggers the post_save signal (sync_user_group, connected in apps.py) that puts them in their role’s Group. That Group’s permissions are what has_perm() checks against in _can_edit_article/_can_delete_article, and what makes ‘editor1’ actually behave like an editor in these tests.

NewsletterViewTestCase and ArticleApprovalNotificationTestCase use plain Django TestCase + the session-based test client, since newsletters and article approval are HTML views, not part of the REST API.

class ArticlesAndMore.tests.ArticleApprovalNotificationTestCase(methodName='runTest')[source]

Bases: TestCase

Verifies that approving an article — the not-approved -> approved transition inside article_approve — triggers both approval side effects: the subscriber email and the POST to /api/approved/. The external POST is always mocked, since letting it run for real would mean the Django test client (which isn’t a real listening server) attempting a genuine network connection on every approval. The email doesn’t strictly need mocking (Django’s test runner already swaps in an in-memory backend automatically) but mocking notify_article_approved directly is the simplest way to confirm article_approve calls it at all, independent of what it does internally.

ArticlesAndMore.views.api_approved(request)[source]

Stands in for a third-party ‘article received’ endpoint. Real external integrations wouldn’t hold a Django session or CSRF token, so this view is intentionally exempt from CSRF and open to any POST — logs whatever payload it receives and echoes it back.

ArticlesAndMore.views.article_approve(request, pk)[source]

Toggle an article’s approved status. Editors only. When an article is newly approved (not when it’s unapproved), notify subscribers by email and share it via the internal /api/approved endpoint.

ArticlesAndMore.views.article_create(request)[source]

Create an article. Journalists may select any publisher, or leave it unset to publish independently.

ArticlesAndMore.views.article_delete(request, pk)[source]

Delete an article. Editors may delete any article; journalists may only delete articles they wrote themselves.

ArticlesAndMore.views.article_detail(request, pk)[source]

Show a single article. Readers may only view approved articles from a publisher or journalist they’re subscribed to (same rule as article_list); journalists and editors can view any article.

ArticlesAndMore.views.article_list(request)[source]

List articles. Readers see only approved articles from publishers or journalists they follow; journalists and editors see everything.

ArticlesAndMore.views.article_update(request, pk)[source]

Update an article. Editors may update any article; journalists may only update articles they wrote themselves.

ArticlesAndMore.views.journalist_list(request)[source]

List all journalists. Readers can subscribe/unsubscribe from here.

ArticlesAndMore.views.newsletter_create(request)[source]

Create a newsletter. Only approved articles can be added to a newsletter. Journalists may select any publisher, or leave it unset to publish independently.

ArticlesAndMore.views.newsletter_delete(request, pk)[source]

Delete a newsletter. Restricted to users with the delete_newsletters permission (Journalists and Editors).

ArticlesAndMore.views.newsletter_detail(request, pk)[source]

Show a single newsletter. Readers may only view newsletters from a publisher or journalist they’re subscribed to (same rule as newsletter_list); journalists and editors can view any newsletter. Within the newsletter, readers only see its approved articles.

ArticlesAndMore.views.newsletter_list(request)[source]

List newsletters. Readers see only newsletters from publishers or journalists they follow; journalists and editors see everything.

ArticlesAndMore.views.newsletter_update(request, pk)[source]

Update a newsletter. Restricted to users with the change_newsletters permission (Journalists and Editors).

ArticlesAndMore.views.publisher_assign_journalist(request, pk)[source]

The publisher’s own editor assigns an unassigned journalist to it. GET shows a form with a dropdown of journalists with no publisher yet (see AssignJournalistForm); POST assigns the selected one.

ArticlesAndMore.views.publisher_assign_self(request, pk)[source]

An unassigned editor joins an existing publisher as one of its editors. Multiple editors can share the same publisher — publisher_e is many-to-many.

ArticlesAndMore.views.publisher_create(request)[source]

Create a new publisher. Restricted to editors who aren’t already assigned to one — creating a publisher automatically assigns the creating editor to it, and publisher_e is a single field, so an editor can only belong to one publisher at a time.

ArticlesAndMore.views.publisher_detail(request, pk)[source]

Show a single publisher: its editors, journalists, and articles. Readers can subscribe/unsubscribe here; an unassigned editor can join; the publisher’s own editor(s) can manage its journalists or leave.

ArticlesAndMore.views.publisher_leave(request, pk)[source]

An editor leaves the publisher they’re currently assigned to.

ArticlesAndMore.views.publisher_list(request)[source]

List all publishers. Readers can subscribe/unsubscribe from here.

ArticlesAndMore.views.publisher_remove_journalist(request, pk, journalist_id)[source]

The publisher’s own editor removes one of its journalists, freeing that journalist up to be assigned elsewhere.

ArticlesAndMore.views.toggle_journalist_subscription(request, pk)[source]

Subscribe/unsubscribe the current reader to a journalist.

ArticlesAndMore.views.toggle_publisher_subscription(request, pk)[source]

Subscribe/unsubscribe the current reader to a publisher.
